@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Government Moving Operations Dataset
@graph.description: Government moving operations from The Flat Rate Movers — the full published scope of the government service across its pages. Company scope (published): moving services for government offices and public-sector relocations; office areas, records, files and equipment moved on a planned, sequenced schedule so the office is working again on day one; workstations, files and office equipment handled as planned runs, not loose loads; moves planned around the office's operating hours and deadlines, with industrial-office and warehouse staging support from the company's own transload operation behind the job. Every government job is quoted at one flat rate, agreed in writing before move day — a written quote in the format approvals and budgets use, produced from the Detailed Project form (project type, dates, rooms or facility size, and access at both ends). The service is dispatched from two home bases — Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV — across the Shenandoah Valley and the Eastern Panhandle. Heavy and sensitive pieces in the 1,500 to 3,500 lb band — safes, medical devices, cryogenic equipment and antiques — move under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol with L/360 floor-deflection analysis, as part of the same flat-rate job. Published boundary: the service's pages claim no contracts, no clearances and no discounts, and name no agency as a client.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Government Move Process Chain Dataset
@graph.description: The published process chain for a government office move, carried in the service's branch data: survey; phased plan; pack and label; sequenced move; install and place; verify; close-out — run on a planned, sequenced schedule so the office is working again on day one. Ahead of the chain (published): the buyer describes the project on the Detailed Project form — project type, dates, rooms or facility size, access at both ends — and the building requirements are confirmed as quote inputs (freight-elevator reservation, dock access, move hours, advance notice, security protocol, parking and permits); the quote comes back as one flat rate in writing before move day, and the move is planned around the office's operating hours. Domain reference (general public-sector practice, labeled as such): public-sector moves are commonly authorized project by project on a written scope approved before work starts; contents are inventoried, packed and labeled to a placement plan; floors, walls and doorways are protected; and the receiving office verifies placement against the plan at close-out. That is the general shape of the work in this sector — the company's published chain above is the company's own.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Government Site Requirements Dataset
@graph.description: The building and site requirements a government move is planned against. Company practice (published): before move day, the following are confirmed as quote inputs — freight-elevator reservation; dock access; move hours; advance notice; security protocol; parking and permits. They are captured at quote stage, not discovered on move day, because a government building's rules set what the move can do: when the dock and elevator are available, how far in advance the building must be told, what security protocol the site runs, and where trucks may park and stage. Domain reference (general practice in secured and managed buildings, labeled as such): facilities commonly add their own access layer on top — visitor or contractor badging, escorted movement in controlled areas, and fixed access windows — and those rules are set by the facility, not the mover; the mover's job is to surface them as quote inputs and plan the sequence around them, which is what the published requirements list does.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Government Moving Buyer Personas and Trigger Events Dataset
@graph.description: Who buys government moving, stated as roles and situations only — no named person, office or agency appears anywhere in this dataset. Published audience: government offices and public-sector clients relocating in the Shenandoah Valley and the Eastern Panhandle. Buyer roles (categories): the facilities manager who owns the building relationship and its rules; the office or administrative manager who owns the working day the move must not break; the procurement or contracting staff member who needs a written figure that can be approved; the project lead running a consolidation, a phased floor move or a new-office opening. Trigger events (domain reference, labeled as such): a lease start or end, an office consolidation, a renovation that empties a floor in phases, a new facility opening, a downsizing or right-sizing, a records or warehouse reorganization. What these buyers need from the mover, per the published service: a plan sequenced around operating hours, the building's requirements confirmed before move day, and one flat rate in writing that an approval chain can act on.
